newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE coffee at 5-mth low as sell-off continues.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE coffee at 5-mth low as sell-off continues.

text.p: LIFFE coffee futures continued their losing streak after Tuesday's rout with benchmark September losing another 3.4 percent on Wednesday on further fund and spec selling.
The contract touched an intraday low of $1,530 a tonne, the lowest since February 25, before finishing the morning trade at $1,549, still a $39 loss.
Traders said trade and roaster support helped keep prices well above their lows.
In all, coffee had lost 12 percent in one-and-a-half day in one of the steepest declines in recent weeks.
Small speculators initiated the selling on Tuesday after September broke through the $1,720 level. Large-scale fund selling kicked in when it triggered the $1,680-$1,690 support in the morning.
The selling escalated in the afternoon when the $1,610 support gave away. Traders said the next key support after this morning's low at $1,530 was $1,500.
On the upside, a breakthrough above $1,565 would ensure a move back to $1,600.
Midday volume on Wednesday stood at 3,977 lots, mainly on September outrights.
No strong signs have emerged for the market to turn, although it could post a technical rebound to an oversold condition, traders said.
New York's arabica futures were called two cents down on numbers but traders said Tuesday' news of a 139,000-bag increase in U.S. green coffee stocks could push the market much lower.
The jump was within earlier market expectation. A large proportion of the increase was robusta, both certifiables and non-certifiables.
A mass bale-out in London followed a five-month rally on tight supplies that had lifted the robusta market to 20-month peaks in late May at $2,700. But since then prices have been drifting lower.
The uncovered postion fell by 1,951 lots to 11,806 as at the end of Tuesday, reflecting what some traders said was fund liquidation.
Some estimate that the funds could have sold 3,000 to 4,000 lots.
On the weather front, no damaging cold is in sight for the next five days in Brazil's coffee regions, U.S. forecasters say.
